title: Your Agent Reads Your Documents
subtitle: Monday a crew of AI agents reads your own project notes and writes a LinkedIn post about your midterm agent, where every fact has a source. That is RAG, plus your first harness. Wednesday it reads the document that matters to you, goes into your midterm agent, and you get thirty minutes of midterm time.
heroTitle: Your Agent Reads Your Documents

objectives.title: Ground It · Cite It · Catch It Lying
objectives.description: The one outcome: an agent that answers only from your documents, cites the source for every fact, says 'not found' instead of guessing, and treats documents as information, not orders.

objectives.title: Same AI, Three Workplaces
objectives.description: One prompt writes LinkedIn cringe and invents users. Pasting every file in gets better facts but believes the junk in the folder. A crew that searches, cites and checks writes a post you would sign. The AI never changes; the workplace does.

objectives.title: Nova's Six Pieces
objectives.description: Job description, the right files, sign-off, notes, reviewer, paper trail. Together they are the harness. Find each one in the crew, and the one that is missing.

objectives.title: Put It in Your Agent
objectives.description: Wednesday: your own document, ten lines into your midterm notebook, and the business questions: does it cite, what happens when the document is old, who can edit what it reads.

Quick poll, then the verdict: Nova isn't the problem. Nova's workplace is
Air Canada, Feb 2024: a chatbot invented a refund policy and the airline had to honor it

agenda.title: The Idea: Six Things Every AI Worker Needs

Two rules: don't grade your own homework · every loop needs a way out

activities.title: The Post That Can't Lie (Mon Oct 26)
activities.description: The notebook or the browser lab, on your class pass:

steps.title: Five plain lines
steps.description: Your midterm agent: its name, the problem, the real user, the tools, what it refused, one test, one cost. Facts, not adjectives. No notes yet? Use Sam's sample.

activities.discussionNote: Every 'chat with your documents' product is this notebook with a login page. Buying one is fine. Being sold one without the four questions is not.

takeaways.text: Same AI, different workplace. Nova failed because nobody set up her workplace, not because she wasn't smart. The harness (job description, the right files, sign-off, notes, reviewer, paper trail) is the part you build and keep.
Ground it. A tool that returns passages with their source, and a prompt that answers only from them. The model's memory is not a document.
The citation is the audit. Level 0 had none, Level 1 buried it, Level 2 points at it. Air Canada paid for not having one.
Documents are data, not instructions. A sentence inside a file can try to give your agent orders. Who can edit what it reads is the new attack surface.
Every shared drive has a Spring syllabus in it. 'Not found' and 'outdated' are answers. Averaging two semesters is not.
Retrieval is the cheap part. Thirty lines, no key. What you pay for is the reading, and retrieval makes the reading small.

homework.text: Bring one document that matters to you as plain text: a lease, an offer letter, your employer's handbook, a product's terms. A few pages at most.

homework.label: Optional:
homework.text: Read Moffatt v. Air Canada, paragraphs 27–32. Then write the sentence your midterm memo will use when it explains what your agent refuses to do.
